items.title: Ashura commemorates Husayn's martyrdom at Karbala
items.claim: What is the significance of Ashura in Shia Islam?

options.text: A celebration of victory in battle
Commemoration of the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali (grandson of Muhammad) at Karbala on 10 Muharram 61 AH (10 October 680 CE) — a defining event of Shia identity, marked with mourning rituals

items.reveal:
Husayn, his family and 72 followers refused allegiance to the Umayyad caliph Yazid I and were besieged then killed at Karbala (in modern Iraq). The event is recounted in detail in Shia narrative tradition (maqtal literature).

Muharram processions (matam) in Shia communities involve mourning, recitation, sometimes ritualised self-flagellation (different observances by region; many Shia clerics prefer blood donation as a modern alternative).

In Sunni Islam, 10 Muharram is also significant — Muhammad observed the day as a fast, having found Jewish residents of Medina fasting in commemoration of Moses's deliverance. Sunni observance is much quieter than Shia.
items.why: Religious calendars carry historical memory. Ashura, like Pesach, ritualises a specific historical wound — and the difference in how Sunnis and Shias mark the same date reveals the structural differences between the branches.

items.title: Ten human Sikh Gurus, then the eternal Guru Granth Sahib
items.claim: How does the Sikh tradition handle leadership after Guru Gobind Singh?

options.text: It ended with the tenth Guru with no continuation
In 1708 Guru Gobind Singh declared the Guru Granth Sahib (the scripture) to be the eternal Guru — no further human gurus
It continues through a hereditary line

items.reveal:
Guru Gobind Singh died in 1708 from a stab wound inflicted by an Afghan assassin. Before his death he installed the Adi Granth (compiled by Guru Arjan in 1604) as Guru Granth Sahib — making the scripture the eternal Guru.

The Guru Granth Sahib (1,430 pages, mostly in Gurmukhi script) contains hymns by six of the ten Gurus, plus 15 Hindu and Muslim saints (bhagats) — including Kabir and Sheikh Farid. It is treated as a living Guru: bowed to, awakened in the morning, put to rest at night.

Sikh gurdwaras place the Guru Granth Sahib on a throne (palki) as the central focus.
items.why: The structural innovation of designating scripture as eternal Guru ended succession disputes that plague many religions. Sikh community continuity rests on the text, not on a living hierarchy.

items.title: Dharma is a central but multi-layered Hindu concept

options.text: A complex term combining duty, righteousness, cosmic order and the proper way of life — context-specific (sva-dharma, one's own duty), stage-of-life-specific (ashrama dharma), and universal (sanatana dharma)

items.reveal:
The root dhr- means 'to hold' or 'sustain'. Dharma includes the cosmic order (rita in Vedic terms), social duty (varna dharma — duties of one's caste), age-appropriate duty (ashrama dharma — student, householder, forest-dweller, renouncer), and universal moral law (sanatana dharma).

The Bhagavad Gita (around 2nd century BCE) is the most influential text on dharma. Arjuna's crisis on the battlefield turns on the conflict between his duty as warrior (his sva-dharma) and his reluctance to kill kinsmen.

Krishna teaches that performing one's dharma without attachment to results (karma yoga) is the path to liberation.
items.why: Dharma has no single English equivalent. Translating it as 'religion' or 'duty' alone misses the richness — it shapes how Hindus understand both individual choice and cosmic order.
